description: Use this when someone asks why their TikTok views dropped, or whether the views of a public TikTok account have gone down. Input: the TikTok username. It compares the median views of the 5 newest public videos that are at least 3 days old with the median of the videos before them and says whether that is a big drop (under half of usual). The result keeps what was observed apart from possible causes: the causes are general possibilities to check, not findings. Videos from the last 3 days are left out because they are still collecting views. It only compares public view counts: it cannot see TikTok’s internal account status and does not confirm any restriction. It needs at least 8 public videos that are 3 days old or older.

username.description: Required. The public TikTok username to read, as text, with or without @ (for example nasa), or a tiktok.com profile link.

name: check_tiktok_view_drop

big_drop.description: true when the median views of the 5 newest videos that are at least 3 days old are under half of the median of the videos before them.

message.description: One or two plain sentences that say what was found or what went wrong.

observed.description: What the public numbers show. These are the facts.

possible_causes.description: General possibilities to check, listed only when there is a big drop. Not findings: this data cannot show which one applies.

status.description: ok, or the plain reason there is no result (not_found, private, no_videos, videos_unavailable, not_enough_videos, invalid_input, unknown_niche, niche_needed, no_data, rate_limited, paused, off, busy, unavailable).

videos_left_out_as_too_new.description: Videos posted in the last 3 days, left out because they are still collecting views.

title: Check a TikTok account for a drop in views
